full.rationale: Rust payload rebaselined 2026-08-08 for 1.8.4: +287,744 bytes over the 1.7.5 reference, which overran the previous 256 KiB allowance by 25,600 bytes. The growth is the 1.8.x work measured against a 1.7.5 baseline, not one release's worth: the QuickLook-parity preview batch and its transport strip, the SQLite database view, the portable registration path, and 1.8.4's own additions - the icon-style format badge (src/badge.rs: a seven-tint category palette and the dog-eared page silhouette), src/checkerpx.rs, src/typeoverlay.rs, and three new doctor checks including the shell round-trip that finally distinguishes 'our decoder works but Explorer drops it' (issue #16). The INSTALLER reference moved with it, to 1.8.4: the compressed setup grew 132,710 bytes over the 1.7.5 reference and overran the 128 KiB allowance by 1,638 bytes, which is the same Rust growth after compression and not a new payload. The magick budget is UNCHANGED and was not what tripped. The 1.7.5 rationale (the from-scratch JPEG 2000 reduced-resolution decoder in src/decode/jp2) still holds and is still in this payload. Keep later releases within 128 KiB compressed and 256 KiB for each raw payload unless an explicit reviewed policy change records why.

ARM64 Rust payload rebaselined 2026-08-06 for 1.8.0. The old reference was still 1.6.0-arm64-full-stubbed (20,234,240 bytes) while x64 was rebaselined at 1.7.5, so this is THREE releases of accumulated, already-reviewed growth measured against a stale baseline, not a sudden jump: +299,520 bytes total, which overran the 256 KiB allowance by 37,376 bytes. The growth is the same reviewed work x64 already absorbed (the from-scratch JPEG 2000 reduced-resolution decoder in src/decode/jp2 at 1.7.5, the native DDS BC1-BC7 tier at 1.7.3) plus 1.8.0's own additions: the portable file-backed settings store, the doctor report window and its four new checks, and the shared email rule. Installer and magick budgets are UNCHANGED and were not what tripped. ARM64 FULL, text-stack STUBBED, recalibrated 2026-08-02. ARM64 bundles the same pinned ImageMagick 7.1.2-29 Q16-HDRI release as x64 (packaging/imagemagick-source-arm64.json) and now also stubs the text-shaping stack the way x64 does, so the two architectures are at parity: magick payload 29217728 bytes here against x64's 29,827,612. Installer 12146914 bytes, SHA-256 bfed8d336c8ee82fc6043bd9ae4b4274596c4d804fa385c9a726fd709d2168f2. The stubs are built with the MSVC ARM64 toolchain (cl + link /DEF /IMPLIB) rather than MinGW, because MinGW emits x86_64 PEs regardless of target - the first ARM64 Full build silently replaced genuine ARM64 DLLs with x64 stubs, which an ARM64 loader refuses. gendef still extracts the exports for both architectures, since a PE export table is architecture-independent. link's /IMPLIB is load-bearing: without it the linker drops <name>.lib and <name>.exp beside /OUT, straight into the shipped bundle. harfbuzz and fribidi end up fully pruned once stubbing removes their importers, which is why the file count is 155. Every staged PE is asserted to be machine 0xAA64. NOTE: published 1.6.0 shipped the UNSTUBBED arm64 payload (13,589,408-byte installer); this reference applies from the next release.
